legend: You are given a permutation†%%ZSMJ0%% a%%ZSMJ1%% of size n%%ZSMJ2%%. We call an index i%%ZSMJ3%% good if ai=i%%ZSMJ4%% is satisfied. After each second, we rotate all indices that are not good to the right by one position. Formally,

Let s1,s2,…,sk%%ZSMJ5%% be the indices of a%%ZSMJ6%% that are not good in increasing order. That is, sj<sj+1%%ZSMJ7%% and if index i%%ZSMJ8%% is not good, then there exists j%%ZSMJ9%% such that sj=i%%ZSMJ10%%.
For each i%%ZSMJ11%% from 1%%ZSMJ12%% to k%%ZSMJ13%%, we assign as(i%k+1):=asi%%ZSMJ14%% all at once.
For each i%%ZSMJ15%% from 1%%ZSMJ16%% to n%%ZSMJ17%%, find the first time that index i%%ZSMJ18%% becomes good.

†%%ZSMJ19%% A permutation is an array consisting of n%%ZSMJ20%% distinct integers from 1%%ZSMJ21%% to n%%ZSMJ22%% in arbitrary order. For example, [2,3,1,5,4]%%ZSMJ23%% is a permutation, but [1,2,2]%%ZSMJ24%% is not a permutation (2%%ZSMJ25%% appears twice in the array) and [1,3,4]%%ZSMJ26%% is also not a permutation (n=3%%ZSMJ27%% but there is 4%%ZSMJ28%% in the array).
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t%%ZSMJ29%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ30%%). The description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ31%% (1≤n≤106%%ZSMJ32%%) — the size of permutation a%%ZSMJ33%%.
The second line of each test case contains n%%ZSMJ34%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ35%% (1≤ai≤n%%ZSMJ36%%) — the elements of permutation a%%ZSMJ37%%.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ38%% over all test cases does not exceed 106%%ZSMJ39%%.
output: For each test case, output a single line containing n%%ZSMJ40%% integers where the i%%ZSMJ41%%-th integer represents the first time that index i%%ZSMJ42%% becomes good.
note: In the first test case, 2%%ZSMJ43%% and 5%%ZSMJ44%% are already in the correct position so indices 2%%ZSMJ45%% and 5%%ZSMJ46%% become good at 0%%ZSMJ47%% second. After 1%%ZSMJ48%% second, a cyclic shift will be done with s=[1,3,4]%%ZSMJ49%%, resulting in array a=[1,2,3,4,5]%%ZSMJ50%%.
